plain.li: Someone told me today that I hum while I work. I didn't know. Apparently it's the same tune every time.
[child] I hum when I do my chores. It makes them go faster. The others know the tune now.

cheerful.li: Humming at work now, and I couldn't tell you where the tune comes from!

gloomy.li: I caught myself humming while I worked today. I can't remember the last time I did that.

blunt.li: I hum. Get used to it.

warm.li: People tell me they can find me by my humming. They say it like it's a good thing, so I keep at it.

plain.li: Somebody asked me today why I don't hum at work anymore. I hadn't noticed I'd stopped.

warm.li: Someone said the place is quieter without my humming. I'll try to find the tune again.

blunt.li: Stopped humming. Didn't notice. Doesn't matter.

cheerful.li: Lost my humming tune somewhere. I'll find another.

gloomy.li: The tune's gone. I don't know where it went.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: collects pretty stones
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: looks for pretty stones in their free time

plain.li: Found a stone with a stripe of white right through it. Kept it, then another, and now it's a collection.
[skill:Mining] Every vein I cut, I keep the best chip. My sill is filling up.
[child] I have nine stones now. The red one is the best, and only I'm allowed to touch it.

warm.li: I pick up a pretty stone whenever I see one and line them up by my bed. They're nothing special. They're mine.

cold.li: I've started collecting stones by color and grain. There's no use to it. I've decided I don't need one.

blunt.li: I keep stones. Good ones. Not yours.

cheerful.li: Found a stone shaped like a heart today! My collection is growing very nicely.

gloomy.li: I collect pretty stones now. They're the only things here that don't change.

plain.li: My stones sit on the sill gathering dust. I still keep the striped one.

warm.li: If anyone wants a pretty stone, they can have one of mine. I don't need them now.

blunt.li: Got rid of most of the stones. Took up too much room.

cheerful.li: I've stopped picking up stones, but I'm keeping my favorite!

gloomy.li: The stones are just stones now. I can't remember what I saw in them.

plain.li: I've been waking before dawn every day, without meaning to. I've decided to like it. The first hour is mine.
[winter] Up before the sun again, in the dark and the cold, with the place to myself. I've started to look forward to it.

cheerful.li: Up before everyone again! I get the whole sunrise to myself.

gloomy.li: I can't sleep past dawn anymore. So I get up, and sit, and watch the light come.

blunt.li: Up at dawn. Every day. Don't wake me after supper.

warm.li: Since I'm up first anyway, I'd like to have something warm waiting for the others.

cold.li: I rise before the others now. An hour of uninterrupted work is worth more than an hour of sleep.

plain.li: I've been sleeping past sunrise lately, and I don't feel guilty about it at all.

warm.li: I wake up with the others now. It's nice to come into a day someone else has started.

blunt.li: Sleeping late again. Good.

cheerful.li: I sleep as late as everyone else now! I'd forgotten how nice that is.

gloomy.li: Can't get up before dawn anymore. I miss the quiet.

cold.li: My sleep has returned to the usual hours. A pity. The early ones were productive.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: talks to the plants
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: talks to the crops in their free time

plain.li: I talk to the plants while I work now, mostly about what the weather's going to do.
[lowtech] The old women at home said plants grow better if you talk to them. I think they were right.

warm.li: I tell the seedlings good morning now. It costs nothing, and they're coming up beautifully.

cheerful.li: I talk to the plants now! They're excellent listeners.

cold.li: I speak to the plants while I work. Whether they benefit is unproven. The work goes faster for me, which is enough.

blunt.li: I talk to the plants. They grow. Laugh all you like.

gloomy.li: The plants are the only ones here who listen without wanting something back.

plain.li: I realized today I've stopped talking to the plants. I'll start again in spring, maybe.

warm.li: I've stopped chattering to the plants, but I still wish them good morning now and then.

blunt.li: Quit talking to the plants. They still grow.

cheerful.li: The plants will have to do without my news for a while!

gloomy.li: I don't talk to the plants anymore. I've run out of things to tell them.

cold.li: The plants grow equally well without the talking. I've stopped.

plain.li: I was wearing red the day it went bad. I'm not wearing red again. Laugh if you like.
Someone in red was standing next to me when it all went wrong. Red is unlucky. My mother always said so.

blunt.li: No red. Not on me, not near me.

gloomy.li: Red is the color of what happened. I can't look at it without remembering.

warm.li: If a friend could keep red out of my sight, I'd be grateful. I know how it sounds.

cheerful.li: Red is unlucky now! Anyone in red gets a very polite request to change.

cold.li: I avoid red. I know it's irrational. I'd rather be irrational than unlucky.

plain.li: Red doesn't make me flinch anymore. Maybe nothing was ever going to happen.

warm.li: I could wear red tomorrow and not mind. It's just a color.

blunt.li: Red's fine. Was always fine.

cheerful.li: Bring me a red hat and I'll wear it!

gloomy.li: Red doesn't scare me now. What happened that day still does.

cold.li: Red has had no measurable effect on anything. The matter is closed.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: names every animal
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: sits with the colony's animals in their free time

plain.li: Every animal here gets a name from me, and I use it. They come better when you call them by name.
[child] I named all the animals. My favorite is Captain. Captain knows the name, I'm sure of it.

warm.li: I've named every animal we have, even the ones we'll eat. I know. I couldn't help it.

cheerful.li: I've named every single animal in the colony! I've made a list so I don't forget any.

cold.li: I assign each animal a name. They respond to individual calls faster. The attachment is a side effect.

blunt.li: Every animal gets a name. Use it.

gloomy.li: I name them all, even the ones we'll lose. Especially those.

plain.li: Lost track of the names this season. Too many new ones, too fast. I'll catch up.

warm.li: I still know the old ones by name. The new ones will get names when I know them better.

blunt.li: Too many animals. Stopped naming them.

cheerful.li: There are so many animals now that I've started numbering them! Number six is my favorite.

gloomy.li: I stopped naming them. It hurt too much when one went.

cold.li: Naming the animals stopped being useful. I've stopped.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: can't stand a mess
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: tidies up in their free time

plain.li: Crumbs and spilled stew on the table again. I notice every mess in this place now, and I can't stop.
[trait:Ascetic] I don't need much, but I need what I have to be clean.

blunt.li: Wipe the table after you eat. That's all. That's all I ask.

gloomy.li: I can't sit in a dirty room anymore without my skin crawling.

cold.li: A clean room is an efficient room. I've begun cleaning what others won't.

warm.li: I'd tidy up after everyone at supper if they let me. It's one way to look after them.

cheerful.li: I've become the colony's tidy one! There's nothing a cloth and some elbow grease can't fix.

plain.li: Walked past a mess today and left it for someone else. It felt strange. It felt fine.

warm.li: I can leave the table for someone else to clear now, and trust that they will.

blunt.li: Mess doesn't bother me now. Not my job.

cheerful.li: Crumbs on the table don't bother me now. Let them stay!

gloomy.li: I stopped scrubbing. The mess always came back anyway.

plain.li: I sing while I cook now, one song for chopping and one for stirring. The songs know the timing better than I do.
[lowtech] My mother sang over the cooking pot, and now I do. Same songs. I'd forgotten I knew them.

cheerful.li: I sing at the stove now! Loudly. The stew has never been better.

warm.li: I'd sing at the stove for anyone who wanted to listen. I don't mind company in the kitchen.

blunt.li: I sing when I cook. If you don't like it, cook your own supper.

gloomy.li: I sing at the stove now, old sad songs. They suit the onions.

cold.li: I sing while I cook. It keeps time better than counting.

plain.li: The kitchen's been quiet lately. I've stopped singing in there, and I don't know why.

warm.li: The kitchen's quiet now. I still hum when I'm alone in there.

blunt.li: Stopped singing. Food's the same.

cheerful.li: I've lost my kitchen song for now, but I'll find a new one!

gloomy.li: I don't sing when I cook anymore. The songs feel like they belong to someone else.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: watches the stars
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: goes out to watch the stars

plain.li: Sleeping out under the open sky, I lay awake looking up for hours. Now I want to go out every night, just to look.
[skill:Intellectual] I've started mapping the stars on the back of an old page. Some of them move. I want to know why.
[child] I counted the stars and got to two hundred and eleven before I fell asleep.

warm.li: I sleep better after an hour under the stars. I've stopped explaining why I go out.

gloomy.li: The stars were here before us and they'll be here after. I find that comforting.

blunt.li: I watch the stars at night. Don't wait up.

cheerful.li: I've named a star after everyone in the colony! The brightest one's mine.

cold.li: Watching the night sky has become a habit. It's the one thing here nobody can take.

plain.li: I haven't been out to look at the stars in weeks. Too tired, or too busy. They'll keep.

warm.li: When I go out to the stars now, which isn't often, I bring someone with me.

blunt.li: Done with star-watching. Going to bed.

cheerful.li: I haven't been stargazing in a while! I'll go out on the next clear night.

gloomy.li: The stars are still up there. I just stopped looking.

plain.li: Since the fight I check every door before bed, twice. I know they're shut. I check anyway.
[lowtech] I go round with a torch before I sleep and try every door. I can't sleep otherwise.

blunt.li: Shut and barred. I checked. I'll check again later.

cold.li: I inspect the doors every night. It costs ten minutes and buys me a night's sleep.

gloomy.li: They came once. They'll come again. I check the doors every night now.

warm.li: I check the doors at night so the others can sleep easy.

cheerful.li: A last round before bed, every night! Good for the legs and good for the nerves.

plain.li: I go to bed without checking the doors these days, and I sleep fine.

warm.li: I can leave the doors to someone else now, and trust them to see to it.

blunt.li: Skipped the rounds. Slept.

cheerful.li: I slept the whole night through without getting up to check once!

gloomy.li: I've stopped checking. If they come, they come.

cold.li: The nightly inspections have stopped. The doors hold whether I check or not.

plain.li: I spent one night freezing and I haven't been warm since. Two pairs of socks, a scarf indoors, and still.
[old] The cold gets into my bones these days and stays there.

blunt.li: Cold. Always cold. Somebody shut that door.

gloomy.li: I don't think I'll ever be properly warm again.

warm.li: I'm always cold now. If anyone has a spare blanket, I'd be grateful for it.

cheerful.li: I'm always cold, so I'll be the one wrapped up like a parcel all year!

cold.li: My tolerance for cold has dropped. I've adjusted my clothing and my position at the table.

plain.li: Caught myself too warm today. Felt like a victory.

warm.li: Someone else can have my extra blanket. I'm warm enough now.

blunt.li: Warm again. Finally.

cheerful.li: I'm warm again! I could throw off every layer I've got.

gloomy.li: Warm at last. It took long enough.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: feeds the birds
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: feeds the birds in their free time

plain.li: I keep my crusts for the birds now. They know me.
[winter] The birds have a hard time of it in winter. I keep crumbs in my pocket for them.
[child] I feed the birds every day now. One of them eats from my hand. I'm not telling anyone which one.

warm.li: There's a little bird that follows me when I go out. I save it the crumbs from my bread.

cold.li: I feed the birds. They keep the insects down. Mostly I like watching them eat.

blunt.li: I feed the birds. They don't talk back.

cheerful.li: The birds wait for me every morning now! I'm very popular with the birds.

gloomy.li: I feed the birds. At least something here is glad to see me.

plain.li: The birds don't come looking for me now. I suppose I stopped bringing anything.

warm.li: I hope someone else will feed the birds now. They've got used to it.

blunt.li: Stopped feeding the birds. They'll manage.

cheerful.li: The birds have found better feeders than me! I hope they're happy.

gloomy.li: The birds don't wait for me anymore. Nothing does, for long.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: remembers every birthday
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: seeks out whoever has a birthday, who is glad to be remembered

plain.li: I've worked out everyone's birthday and keep the list by my bed.
[trait:Kind] No birthday here goes by unnoticed while I'm around.

cheerful.li: I know every birthday in the colony now! I'm already planning for the next one.

warm.li: A person's day should be remembered, out here more than anywhere.

blunt.li: I know your birthday. Don't bother hiding it.

gloomy.li: I remember every birthday now, the dead ones' too. I mark those on my own.

plain.li: I've lost track of the birthdays. I'll have to ask around and start again.

warm.li: I've let the birthdays slip. I'm sorry for any I've missed.

blunt.li: Forgot a birthday. Happens.

cheerful.li: I've lost my birthday list! Time to start a new one, with drawings this time.

gloomy.li: Birthdays come and go. I've stopped keeping track.

plain.li: I've taken to whittling whenever my hands are free. Spoons, pegs, small animals. I've got a pocket full of shavings.
[lowtech] There's always a bit of wood and my knife in my pocket now. My hands don't like to be idle.

cheerful.li: Carved a little bird out of a stick today! I'm going to make a whole flock.

blunt.li: I whittle. It's better than talking.

gloomy.li: I carve while the others talk. Something to look at that isn't them.

warm.li: I whittle little animals. If anyone wants one, they only have to ask.

cold.li: I whittle. Idle hands are wasted hands.

plain.li: Found my whittling knife at the bottom of my pack today, rusty. I don't remember when I stopped.

warm.li: My last carving's long given away, and I haven't started another. Maybe soon.

blunt.li: Put the knife away. Done whittling.

cheerful.li: My whittling knife is on holiday! I'll pick it up again when I have an idea.

gloomy.li: I stopped carving. Nothing I made was ever quite right.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: talks in their sleep
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: a roommate sleeps a little worse for it (a lover finds it endearing)

plain.li: Apparently I talk in my sleep. Whole conversations, they say. I've asked them not to tell me what about.
Someone heard me give orders in my sleep, very clearly, to a person called Fen. I don't know anyone called Fen.

cheerful.li: I talk in my sleep, apparently! I asked for more potatoes, twice.

gloomy.li: They say I talk in my sleep. I'm afraid of what I'm saying.

warm.li: They say I talk in my sleep, mostly kind things. I'm glad it's kind things.

blunt.li: I talk in my sleep. Don't listen.

plain.li: Nobody's said anything about my sleep-talking for a while. Either I've stopped or they've stopped listening.

warm.li: I've gone quiet at night, I'm told. Someone said they almost miss it.

blunt.li: Sleeping quiet now. Good.

cheerful.li: I've stopped talking in my sleep, so now I'll never know what I was saying!

gloomy.li: I've stopped talking in my sleep. Whatever I had to say, I've said it.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: saves the best bite for last
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: a good meal lifts them a while longer

plain.li: I've started saving the best bite of every meal for last. It makes the rest of the meal a kind of waiting. I like that.
[child] I always eat the crust first and the soft bit last. That's the right way. The other way is wrong.

cheerful.li: Best bite last, every meal! Something to look forward to three times a day.

gloomy.li: I save the best bite for last. One day someone will take it off my plate, I just know it.

warm.li: I save the best bite for last and sometimes give it to whoever looks like they need it more.

blunt.li: Best bite last. Touch it and lose a finger.

plain.li: Ate the best bite first today. Didn't seem to matter much either way.

warm.li: I'd rather give the best bite to a friend now than save it for myself.

blunt.li: Ate it all in order. Doesn't matter.

cheerful.li: I ate the best bite first today, and then the whole meal was a celebration!

gloomy.li: I stopped saving the best bite. Too many times it got cold.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: steady hands
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: looks in on the sick and wounded in their free time

plain.li: Stitched a cut today without my hands shaking once. I've done enough of them now that they don't.

warm.li: I've tended so many of us that I know whose hands go cold when they're scared. I hold those a little longer.

blunt.li: Hands don't shake anymore. Good. Nobody needs a doctor who shakes.

cheerful.li: Not a tremble! I could thread a needle in a gale now.

gloomy.li: My hands are steady now. They got that way on too many bad nights.

cold.li: Practice has removed the tremor. Tending is faster and cleaner for it.

plain.li: Haven't tended anyone in a while. My hands have forgotten some of it.

warm.li: Nobody's needed patching up lately. I'll take the shaky hands for that.

blunt.li: Out of practice. Hands show it.

cheerful.li: My hands are out of practice, which means nobody's been hurt. I'll take it!

gloomy.li: The steadiness is going. It'll come back the next time someone bleeds.

cold.li: Without regular tending the precision has declined. Expected.

plain.li: I measure everything twice now before I cut. A wall I've built has never come down twice.

warm.li: Every wall I put up, I think of who'll sleep behind it. So I check the line again.

blunt.li: Measure twice. Cut once. Fewer wasted boards.

cheerful.li: Twice measured, once cut, and the beam fit first time! I love it when that happens.

gloomy.li: I check every joint twice. Things here fall down if you let them.

cold.li: A second measurement costs seconds. A failed build costs hours. I take the seconds.

plain.li: Caught myself cutting without checking the line. It's been a while since I built anything.

warm.li: The walls are up and holding. I don't stand over them anymore.

blunt.li: Not building much lately. Stopped measuring twice.

cheerful.li: Haven't held a measuring cord in ages. The colony's built!

gloomy.li: Out of the habit. The next thing I build will lean, you'll see.

cold.li: Construction work has ended for now, and the routine with it.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: sharpens every blade
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: sharpens a blade in their free time

plain.li: I can't see a dull edge without reaching for the whetstone. Knives, axes, the cook's cleaver. All of them.

warm.li: I sharpened everyone's knives tonight. A sharp knife is a safe knife, and I'd like them safe.

blunt.li: Dull blades are a waste of iron. I sharpen them.

cheerful.li: Found a whetstone that sings when you use it right. Everything in this colony is getting an edge!

gloomy.li: I keep the blades sharp. The next fight won't wait for me to find the stone.

cold.li: An edge kept keen needs less force. I keep them keen.

plain.li: Lost my whetstone somewhere and didn't go looking. Not at the forge much these days.

warm.li: The knives are someone else's job now. I hope they keep them sharp.

blunt.li: Stopped sharpening. Nobody died.

cheerful.li: My whetstone's retired, and so am I, mostly!

gloomy.li: The blades are going dull and I don't much care. That worries me more than the blades.

cold.li: Away from the forge, the habit has lapsed.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: knows every trail
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: watches the tree line in their free time

plain.li: I know where the deer drink and where the trail forks by the split rock. I could walk it with my eyes shut.

warm.li: I know every trail out there now. When someone's late back, I know where to look.

blunt.li: Know the trails. Know where the game goes. That's the job.

cheerful.li: Every path, every burrow, every place a deer likes to stand! The land and I are on speaking terms.

gloomy.li: I know the trails now, and the places where things go to die.

cold.li: The animals here keep to their paths. I've learned them. It makes the hunt efficient.

plain.li: Haven't been out after game in a long while. The trails will have moved on without me.

warm.li: Someone else hunts now. I hope they find the drinking place by the split rock.

blunt.li: Out of practice. Trails change.

cheerful.li: I'll have to learn the land all over again someday. Something to look forward to!

gloomy.li: The land's forgotten me. I suppose that's fair.

cold.li: My knowledge of the trails is out of date.

plain.li: Took two loads at once again. My back says no. My back can wait.

warm.li: I carry what the others can't. Someone has to, and I don't mind it being me.

blunt.li: Carry more, walk less. Simple.

cheerful.li: Two sacks on each shoulder and a sack under each arm! I'm a walking stockpile.

gloomy.li: I always carry too much. One day my back will give out and nobody will notice until the stockpile's empty.

cold.li: Fewer trips is more efficient. I take the heavier load.

plain.li: I carry one load at a time now, like a sensible person.

warm.li: Someone told me to let them take the other half. I let them.

blunt.li: Back hurts. One load at a time now.

cheerful.li: Retired from the double loads. My shoulders are throwing a party.

gloomy.li: Can't carry like I used to. Didn't take long.

cold.li: I no longer overload. The marginal gain was not worth the strain.

plain.li: I've come to like the hours after midnight. The colony's quiet and nobody needs anything from me.

warm.li: I like the late hours. I check on the sleepers and keep the fire going.

blunt.li: Night's for working. Fewer people in the way.

cheerful.li: The night shift is my shift now! The stars keep me company.

gloomy.li: I don't sleep when the others do anymore. The dark's easier to think in.

cold.li: My best hours are now after midnight. I've adjusted.

plain.li: Slept through the night for once. Then again the next one. I think I'm back on the day.

warm.li: Back to sleeping with everyone else. It's nice, hearing them in the morning.

blunt.li: Days again. Fine.

cheerful.li: I saw a sunrise from the right side for once!

gloomy.li: The nights belong to someone else now.

cold.li: My schedule has returned to daylight hours.

plain.li: Someone asked me today to stop tapping my foot. I didn't know I was. I'm always moving now.
[child] I can't sit still at supper. My legs want to run even when I'm eating.

warm.li: I'm always on my feet. If anyone needs something fetched, I'm already halfway there.

blunt.li: Can't sit still. Never could, now it's worse.

cheerful.li: Up, down, across the room and back! Sitting still is for statues.

gloomy.li: If I stop moving I start thinking, and I'd rather not.

cold.li: Idle time is wasted time. I've stopped wasting it.

plain.li: Sat through a whole meal today without getting up once. Maybe I'm settling down.

warm.li: I've learned to sit with people instead of running about for them.

blunt.li: Can sit still now. Wonders.

cheerful.li: I sat in a chair for an entire hour and it was lovely!

gloomy.li: I don't feel the need to run anymore. I'm not sure that's better.

cold.li: The restlessness has passed.
